directed.conceptual_reading: The representation isolates arithmetic cancellation in the fixed weights μ(n)/n^2 and puts all x-dependence into a smooth exponential kernel. That exposes a form that can be compared termwise with a discrete coefficient representation sharing the same weights.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The bridge object is R(x)/x as a Möbius-weighted kernel sum; changing from reciprocal-zeta coefficients to exp(-x/n^2) is the enabling representation change.
directed.boundary_or_failure: Acceleration supplies an exact alternative representation, not a growth estimate for R and not evidence for the Riemann Hypothesis. This span does not derive the acceleration or quantify its convergence gain.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Forward growth transfer from c_k to R(x)
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: States the general equivalence theorem and proves the c_k-to-R direction by combining the exact exponential transform with a coefficient-weight asymptotic for sum k^{-delta}x^k/k!, exposing Poisson smoothing as the source of the exponent shift.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Binomial-to-exponential explanation of c_k approximately equal to R(k)/k
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Rewrites c_k as a Mobius-weighted binomial-kernel sum and approximates (1-1/n^2)^k by exp(-k/n^2), directly matching the accelerated Riesz representation at x=k. This supplies an interpretable de-Poissonization heuristic later made quantitative.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: The exact exponential transform smooths discrete c_k decay into R(x) growth, while the O(k^{-3/2}) integer-sampling error reverses the transfer; the paired mechanisms explain both the one-power exponent shift and the delta<3/2 proof range.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: The reverse transfer is tied to the proved approximation rate and to integer samples; it does not by itself improve the RH-relevant exponent or establish RH.
related_synthesis_entries.title: Poissonization and quantified de-Poissonization as the equivalence mechanism

risk_spans.reason: Numerical-fit setup and page transition motivate but do not establish the kernel mechanism.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The converse transfer is an integer-sampling stability argument: c_k shadows R(k)/k with an O(k^-3/2) error, so a hypothesized decay for the sampled R term survives only while it dominates that error floor.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The appendix estimate used here is |R(k)/k-c_k| <= (3 sqrt(π)/16)k^-3/2+O(k^-2). If R(k)=O(k^(1-δ)), then |c_k| <= Bk^-δ+O(k^-3/2), yielding c_k=O(k^-δ) for δ<3/2.
directed.conceptual_reading: This is quantified de-Poissonization: continuous information is sampled at integers and transferred back to discrete coefficients through a controlled approximation. The error exponent, rather than formal duality alone, determines the range of the reverse implication.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The bridge object is the integer sample R(k)/k, with the approximation error |R(k)/k-c_k| carrying the proof burden.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The available O(k^-3/2) error does not justify the same conclusion at or beyond δ=3/2, and the source separately notes a stricter RH-relevant restriction. This step does not establish any assumed growth bound.
directed.uncertainty: The proof of the error estimate is deferred to the appendix. Fraction placement in formula (26) is risky in the text layer, but the following inequality unambiguously identifies the compared quantities and leading rate.

supported: The span uses |R(k)/k-c_k|<=(3 sqrt(pi)/16)k^-3/2+O(k^-2) together with R(k)=O(k^(1-delta)) to transfer the assumed integer-sample bound to c_k.
The candidate correctly identifies R(k)/k and its approximation error as carrying the reverse implication and does not treat the assumed R bound as proved.
inference: Calling the step quantified de-Poissonization is a defensible interpretation of the integer-sampling approximation.
unsupported_or_imported: The statement that the estimate does not justify the same conclusion 'at or beyond' delta=3/2 is too strong: at delta=3/2 both the assumed term and the error are O(k^-3/2), so the displayed inequality still gives c_k=O(k^-3/2). Only delta>3/2 is blocked by this error rate.
context_or_ocr_risk: Formula (26) has fraction-placement risk, but the subsequent triangle-inequality line disambiguates the compared quantities and the k^-3/2 rate.
missed_mechanism: The candidate misses the endpoint distinction between the source's stated delta<3/2 range and what the displayed big-O estimate itself permits at delta=3/2.
revision_instructions: Replace the endpoint claim with the precise statement that the O(k^-3/2) error prevents transfer of the sharper O(k^-delta) rate for delta>3/2; report separately that the source states its criterion for delta<3/2.
